family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Ask whether the plant is woody and opposite-leaved, then confirm a long 2-valved capsule with many flat winged seeds.
family_diagnostics.habit: Trees, shrubs or woody vines; local anchors are woody climbers.
family_diagnostics.flower: Showy tubular zygomorphic flowers, commonly with 4 didynamous stamens plus a staminode.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a long 2-valved capsule with numerous flattened winged seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Woody habit + opposite compound leaves + winged-seed capsule is the local family shortcut.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Trumpet flowers get attention, but the woody vine and the long capsule full of winged seeds are what really lock Bignoniaceae in.

steps.title: 1 · See the whole trumpet-vine plan
steps.look_for: Woody climbing habit, opposite pinnately compound leaves, and large tubular flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: Combines the strongest vegetative and floral family cues.

steps.title: 2 · Ignore flower color and find the capsule
steps.look_for: A long dry capsule that splits into two valves.
steps.why_it_matters: The fruit is more diagnostic than an orange trumpet flower.

steps.title: 3 · Look at the seeds
steps.look_for: Many thin flattened seeds with broad papery wings.
steps.why_it_matters: Winged seeds inside a long woody-vine capsule strongly support Bignoniaceae.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flower interior
steps.look_for: Four fertile stamens plus a reduced fifth stamen/staminode.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the family to other Lamiales while fruit/habit keeps it separate.

comparisons.title: Bignoniaceae vs Plantaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have bilabiate tubular flowers. Bignoniaceae is commonly woody with long capsules and flat winged seeds; local Penstemon is herbaceous with a smaller ordinary many-seeded capsule.

comparisons.title: Bignoniaceae vs Oleaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be opposite-leaved woody plants; Oleaceae has tiny flowers and samara/drupe fruit rather than huge trumpet flowers and winged-seed capsules.

visual_lesson.caveat: Flower shape alone is not enough; woody architecture and fruit/seed structure are the safest local confirmation.
